Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. If used long-term or for treating SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone Secretion), regular laboratory and medical tests (e.g., complete blood count, kidney and liver function tests, and mineral levels) should be conducted while taking this medication. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Taking outdated demeclocycline can lead to serious illness. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: Demeclocycline is used to treat a variety of bacterial infections, including those causing acne. It belongs to the tetracycline class of antibiotics and is effective only against bacterial infections. It will not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. How to Use: Take this medication orally on an empty stomach, at least one hour before or two hours after a meal, as directed by your doctor, usually 2 to 4 times daily. Take each dose with a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) unless otherwise directed by your doctor. Do not lie down for at least 10 minutes after taking this medication. Avoid taking this medication within 2 to 3 hours of consuming products containing aluminum, calcium, iron, magnesium, zinc, or bismuth subsalicylate (e.g., antacids, quinapril, sucralfate, vitamins/minerals, dairy products like milk or yogurt, or calcium-enriched juice). The dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For optimal results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. If you are using this medication to treat an infection, continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Inform your doctor if your condition persists or worsens. Side Effects: Common side effects may include diarrhea, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, lightheadedness, or rectal discomfort. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Women of childbearing age who are overweight or have a history of IH are at greater risk. If IH develops, it typically resolves after stopping demeclocycline, but there is a risk of permanent vision loss or blindness. This medication may also rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridium difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice. Precautions: Before taking demeclocycline, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other tetracycline medications (e.g., doxycycline, minocycline, tetracycline), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, using machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Demeclocycline may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). This medication may also increase your sensitivity to the sun. This medication should not be used in children under 8 years of age as it may cause permanent tooth discoloration and other issues. Tooth discoloration has also been reported in older children and young adults. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. You should not become pregnant while using demeclocycline, as it may harm an unborn baby. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Demeclocycline may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., some urine tests for sugar), potentially causing false test results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the U.S., call 1-800-222-1222. Storage: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication. Taking outdated demeclocycline can result in serious illness. Important Note: This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product.
